items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I went to see "Big Chief" Moore at his hotel.

ctx.x: One day during the festival, I went to see "Big Chief" Moore at his hotel. Russell is a real indian and the only one I ever knew that played jazz. I didn't know his weight exactly, but roughly guessing, it must have been at the time about 350 pounds. I tqas about 12:30 a.m. when I knocked on his door and he was still in bed. When he asked who was there. I told him and he said:'Just a minute'. I was waiting almost 10 minutes before he finally opened the door.

When I walked into his room, I saw the reason it had taken him so long to come to the door. His bed was about two feet wider than an army cot and the springs and mattress were about five inches from touching the floor. It must have taken "Big Chief" five minutes to get out of bed and five others to put his bath robe on.

Another day during the week of the festival, "Big Boy" Goodie came to my hotel with some people from Switzerland and introduced me to them. One fellow's name was Peter Wydler and the other was Felix Debrit. "Big Boy" had played in Bern, Switzerland, with Glyn Pacque, the altoman I had worked with in Benny Carter's orchestra 1933 band. Pacque is mentioned in this book back in 37 or 38 and he had been able to stay in Switzerland during the war.
